Summarize UCDP fatality estimates

Source: R/aggregate.R
ucdp_fatalities.Rd

ucdp_fatalities() aggregates the low, best, and high fatality estimates while retaining information about incomplete observations. It recognizes common UCDP triplets such as low/best/high and bd_low/bd_best/bd_high.

Usage

ucdp_fatalities(
  data,
  by = NULL,
  low = NULL,
  best = NULL,
  high = NULL,
  na_rm = TRUE,
  missing = c("drop", "error")
)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing fatality estimates.

by

Optional grouping columns.

low, best, high

Optional column names for the three estimates. Supply all three or none. When omitted, common UCDP names are detected.

na_rm

If TRUE, sum the available estimates, but return NA when a group contains no observed value for an estimate. If FALSE, any missing value makes the corresponding group total NA.

missing

How to handle missing grouping values: drop their rows or raise an error.

Value

A tibble containing grouping variables, observation counts, completeness counts, and aggregated low, best, and high estimates.

Examples

events <- data.frame(
  country = c("A", "A", "B"),
  low = c(1, 2, NA), best = c(2, 3, 4), high = c(3, 5, 6)
)
ucdp_fatalities(events)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>   n_observations n_complete n_missing fatalities_low fatalities_best
#>            <int>      <int>     <int>          <dbl>           <dbl>
#> 1              3          2         1              3               9
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: fatalities_high <dbl>
ucdp_fatalities(events, by = "country")
#> # A tibble: 2 × 7
#>   country n_observations n_complete n_missing fatalities_low fatalities_best
#>   <chr>            <int>      <int>     <int>          <dbl>           <dbl>
#> 1 A                    2          2         0              3               5
#> 2 B                    1          0         1             NA               4
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: fatalities_high <dbl>
